preferredPrimitives: existing Threadwise buttons, fields, sheets, cards, and status chips
patterns: dual-orientation desktop weekly timetable with a separate deadline lane
horizontal timetable rows with one weekday label, bounded due rail, then time track
mobile day agenda with explicit schedule editing
persisted collapsible Study sidebar on desktop with an independent mobile drawer
fit-to-window Study image viewer with an explicit natural-resolution inspection mode
theme-aware restrained scrollbars on primary Study navigation and timetable overflow

must: Reuse existing Threadwise tokens and interaction primitives
Keep all task-import controls usable at 360px width
Expose import warnings beside the row they affect
avoid: Decorative gradients or generic AI dashboard cards
Hiding destructive or irreversible import state

decisions.decision: Use one focused TODO review surface with editable rows, explicit inclusion controls, and a sticky Import action.
decisions.reason: Batch parsing is useful only when uncertainty is visible and correctable before shared tasks are created; a single mobile-first surface avoids chat clutter and preserves Threadwise's existing visual language.

decisions.decision: Organize desktop TODO rows into title, metadata, and correction layers, and commit deadline edits only through an explicit Done action.
decisions.reason: The original row mixed unrelated information and immediate API saves repeatedly dismissed the native date-time picker; staged editing preserves focus while one deliberate commit keeps shared state accurate.

decisions.decision: Give private Study a first-class timetable: recurring schedule blocks use a weekly clock grid, while assignment deadlines remain in a separate Work due lane and mobile defaults to a day agenda.
decisions.reason: Study data was already present but settings and chat cards did not reveal the shape of a week. Separating scheduled time from due time keeps the visualization truthful, and the day agenda avoids shrinking seven columns into an unusable mobile layout.

decisions.decision: Let desktop Study users switch the weekly timetable between vertical and horizontal orientations while retaining the same schedule data, deadline shelf, editor, and day agenda.
decisions.reason: Days-as-columns is best for scanning a conventional week, but days-as-rows makes long teaching days and time gaps easier to compare. Orientation is a view preference, not a second scheduling model, and remains hidden on mobile where a day agenda is clearer.

decisions.decision: Give Horizontal Study Timetable one weekday axis and a two-item per-day deadline rail; reserve the week-level Work due shelf for Vertical mode.
decisions.reason: Repeating weekdays across the top and left made the horizontal view look like two calendars overlaid. A bounded adjacent due rail preserves deadline access, communicates its distinction from scheduled time, and moves only genuine overflow into the existing day agenda.

decisions.decision: Use one direct title and no self-evident subtitle on operational pages; reserve one stable daily line for the personal Overview greeting.
decisions.reason: Repeated explanations made simple collections feel generated and increased visual noise. Direct labels preserve hierarchy, while one deterministic Overview line gives the home surface personality without creating layout churn.

decisions.decision: Let laptop and desktop Study users persistently collapse the navigation sidebar while keeping the mobile navigation as an independent drawer.
decisions.reason: Study pages benefit from maximum reading and timetable width, but hiding navigation must remain an explicit reversible preference rather than a breakpoint side effect.

decisions.decision: Open saved Study images fitted to the viewer, then let either the image or a labelled action reveal the natural-resolution image in a full-viewport scrollable canvas.
decisions.reason: Fit mode preserves orientation, while original-pixel inspection makes screenshots and lecture material legible without opening an unsafe external URL or permanently crowding the Library dialog.

decisions.decision: Style desktop Study navigation and horizontal timetable scrollbars with adaptive Threadwise tokens while preserving native scrolling behavior and hiding the drawer scrollbar on mobile.
decisions.reason: These persistent overflow controls are part of the operating surface. Subtle rounded thumbs and brand-tinted hover states keep them legible in both themes without competing with timetable content.
